questions.question_text: Which algorithm is commonly used for supervised learning classification tasks?
options: K-Means Clustering
Support Vector Machines
Principal Component Analysis
Apriori Algorithm
questions.explanation: Support Vector Machines (SVM) is a supervised learning model used for classification and regression analysis.

questions.question_text: What is the primary function of an Operating System's 'scheduler'?
options: Managing memory allocation
Determining which process runs on the CPU and for how long
Converting high-level code to machine language
Managing file permissions
questions.explanation: The CPU scheduler is responsible for assigning processes to the CPU and managing the execution order.

questions.question_text: In computer science, what is the 'Big O' notation primarily used to describe?
options: The physical size of a hard drive
The worst-case time or space complexity of an algorithm
The amount of memory required by the CPU
The network latency of a server
questions.explanation: Big O notation provides a theoretical measure of the execution time or space requirements of an algorithm as input size grows.

questions.question_text: What is the core purpose of a 'Neural Network' hidden layer?
options: To store the final prediction output
To receive the raw input data from sensors
To perform complex transformations on input data to extract features
To display the GUI of the program
questions.explanation: Hidden layers act as the internal processing engine of a neural network, extracting patterns through weighted connections.

questions.question_text: Which of these is a key characteristic of a relational database management system (RDBMS)?
options: Data is stored in unstructured document formats
Data is organized into tables with rows and columns
It cannot be accessed using SQL
It is primarily designed for real-time video streaming
questions.explanation: RDBMS organizes data into relations (tables) that can be linked based on data common to each.

questions.question_text: What does the term 'overfitting' mean in the context of Machine Learning?
options: The model performs poorly on training data
The model learns the noise in training data so well that it fails to generalize to new data
The model requires too much electricity to run
The algorithm is too simple to solve the problem
questions.explanation: Overfitting happens when a model captures specific patterns or noise in training data that do not apply to unseen data.

questions.question_text: In cybersecurity, what is the main purpose of a 'firewall'?
options: To remove viruses from a hard drive
To monitor and control incoming and outgoing network traffic based on security rules
To increase the speed of the internet connection
To backup files to the cloud
questions.explanation: A firewall acts as a barrier between a trusted internal network and an untrusted external network.

questions.question_text: In AI, what is a 'heuristic' search method?
options: A search that guarantees the shortest path
A rule-of-thumb strategy to find solutions more quickly
A method used only in hardware optimization
A random search approach
questions.explanation: Heuristics sacrifice completeness or optimality for speed, allowing an algorithm to find a 'good enough' solution in a large search space.

questions.question_text: What is the primary role of the 'Kernel' in an operating system?
options: Managing user interface aesthetics
Directly interacting with hardware resources
Compiling source code into machine code
Managing internet connectivity protocols
questions.explanation: The kernel is the core of the OS, responsible for CPU scheduling, memory management, and hardware device communication.

questions.question_text: Which data structure follows the 'First-In, First-Out' (FIFO) principle?
options: Stack
Queue
Binary Tree
Hash Map
questions.explanation: A queue is a linear structure where the first element added is the first one removed, similar to a line at a store.
